item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.10
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 10

One call, one set of notes. If Tailwing quits, closes unexpectedly or is reopened while your call is still going, it picks the same meeting up again: one transcript, and notes written once over the whole call. A call that was already split in two can be joined with Join with the Earlier Part.

Notes that read like a document. Finished notes use the reading size with calmer spacing. Decisions have their own section, next steps read as a checklist with each owner's first name, and a line's time shows when you point at it. A decision appears once, without a label in front of it.

Shorter, sharper notes. Bullets are about a fifth shorter. Decisions are listed once, in their own section. People are named instead of written as "Someone". Financial terms like SAFE and Carta are written correctly.

Ask about this meeting. A field at the end of a finished meeting's notes asks about that meeting first, then all of them.

A cleaner meeting header. Transcript, Ask, Folder, Copy and Share sit in the toolbar as real buttons, with Share the main one. A private meeting shows no Copy or Share there; Share and Save, which ask first, are in the options menu.

Calmer during calls. The meeting's page no longer shows the live transcript while a call runs, unless you turn it on in Settings, Meetings. Live translation still shows it. The side panel opens wider.

Steadier when your audio changes. Headphones that connect, disconnect or switch to your phone mid-call no longer freeze Tailwing. Your microphone stays where it is when only your speakers change, and the transcript notes it quietly if the microphone itself changes.

Notes always finish. If writing the notes ever stalls, the meeting says so and offers Try Again. AI tools reading a meeting while its notes are being written are told how far along they are.

Set up next. Set up next only suggests what you haven't connected yet.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.9
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 9

Calls come first. While you're on a call, Tailwing pauses its downloads and background work, and picks them up again when the call ends. It also transcribes at a low priority, so your meeting app gets your Mac first.

A new meeting banner. The banner that offers notes for a call is smaller and clearer. If you also use Parafoil, a new setting, "Let Parafoil take notes when it's running," lets it take the call instead.

Shorter setup. Setup now covers only what your first meeting needs. After your first meeting, Home suggests what to set up next, starting with using your notes in Claude. Everything else is still in Settings.

Better Ask answers. Catch-ups are tighter, and questions about what was settled find the answer more often.

Invites work after setup. An invite link now counts for 30 days after you set up Tailwing, and you can paste one in Settings, Pro. When the friends you invite join, your Pro unlocks within the hour.

Fixes. After a call ends normally, no "Notes stopped" bar stays on screen. The "Tailwing is still running" note appears in the right place on the right display. The offer to take notes closes by itself when the call stops using your microphone. Tailwing keeps taking notes when Granola is also open. Setup no longer lets you skip saving your recovery code. The toolbar shows "Starting…" while notes begin, then Stop.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.8.4
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 8.4

Ask is one conversation. Questions and answers now flow in one chat until you start a new one, and your recent chats are listed so you can go back to them. Sources show as small numbers in the answer, with the full list tucked under it. A suggested question now goes into the box so you can change it before you ask.

Notes appear as they are written. After a meeting, each section of the notes shows up as soon as it is ready, with Transcribing and then Processing shown while you wait.

Settings has more tabs. Translation, People, Ask, and Camera & Screen each have their own tab, so things are easier to find.

Taking notes stays in view. While Tailwing is taking notes, a bar on every other page shows it, with Back to Notes to return. If notes stop without you pressing Stop, Tailwing says why and offers Resume.

Names in one-on-one meetings. In a one-on-one, the live transcript and the notes name the other person, and people who declined the invitation are left out. A meeting linked to a calendar event keeps the event's title.

AirPods and Bluetooth headsets. Tailwing no longer switches your headset into its lower-quality call mode. It uses the microphone your call is using, or your Mac's built-in microphone.

Live translation hears the call's language. Tailwing now picks up the language people are speaking during the call and starts live translation for it.

Cleaner next steps. Notes now drop duplicate and fragment next steps, and in a one-on-one each step goes to the person who took it on.

Camera and Screen Recording setup. New step-by-step guides in Settings, Camera & Screen walk you through allowing Tailwing in macOS and choosing it in your meeting app, and show Ready when everything is set.

Set up before your first meeting. The welcome screen now suggests finishing setup before your first call, and shows how the download is going.

Clearer downloads. One time estimate shows everywhere a download is mentioned, and anything waiting on a download says so.

Fixes. "How are my meetings going?" now gets a catch-up. Amounts like $55k export correctly.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.8.3
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 8.3

Suggested questions. When the Ask box is empty, a few questions sit under it to start from: "Catch me up", "What do I owe people?" and "What changed this week?" across your meetings, or "Summarize this meeting", "What did I agree to?" and "What's still open?" on a meeting. Click one to ask it. They go away as soon as you type.

Ask lists every item. When you ask who was there, which ones, or what the risks are, Ask now lists each one the meetings give, each with its source, instead of stopping at the first.

Ask knows more ways of saying things. Ask also searches for common alternatives to your words, such as price for pricing, or deadline for due.

Ask finds what a person said about a topic. A question about what someone said on a subject now reads the lines near that subject first, including lines where others mention them.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.8.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 8.2

Ask answers broad questions. Ask now answers questions like "what's going on in my meetings" from your most recent meetings, in a sentence or two for each.

Ask follows the conversation. A follow-up such as "and when is that due?" is searched with the question before it. Ask also reads short forms ("abt", "wat"), finds a person from the start of their name, and answers "what do I owe" from your own next steps.

A new Ask box. The Ask field grows as you type, up to six lines. Shift-Return starts a new line, Return sends, and the Send button sits in the box with the meetings it will read.

Ask tells you when it is still getting ready. On a new install, or after a reset, Ask across all your meetings shows how far along the download or the indexing is and asks you to try again in a few minutes. If indexing is paused or has stopped moving, Ask answers from what is indexed and says it may leave some meetings out.

The Screen Recording button adds Tailwing to the list. The Screen Recording button now adds Tailwing to the list in System Settings, so you can switch it on.

Known limits. In long answers across several meetings, Ask can leave out a detail that is in the lines it read, such as a second name in a list. This is next on the list for 8.3.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.8.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 8.2

Notes now stop by themselves when a browser call ends. After a Meet in Chrome, Tailwing could go on taking notes until you stopped it: Chrome kept hold of the microphone, and a normal room is rarely quiet enough for Tailwing to decide the call was over.

This version watches the same signal as the orange microphone dot in your menu bar, so leaving the call ends notes within seconds. If you were only stepping away, the call taking the microphone again within two minutes picks up the same meeting.

The AI tools connector is still paused, as in RC 8.1. It comes back in the next release.
